Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty Final order : All accused are acquitted
Arguments heard on : 12/02/16 Judgment announced on : 12/02/16

Brief facts of the case :
1

In brief, the case of the prosecution is that on 09.01.2016 at about  p.m, Food Inspector V.P.S. Choudhary and Field Assistant Balwant Shah under the supervision and directions of SDM/LHA Sh. K.K. Sharma visited the premises of M/s Sunil Trading Company, where accused Sunil Kumar Goel who was the vendorcum proprietor was found present conducting the business of food articles including the sale of Gutkha, for sale for human consumption and in compliance of the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as the PFA Act & PFA Rules) the Food Inspector collected/ purchased the sample of Gutkha.

2 During the course of investigation, it was revealed that Sh. Sunil Kumar Goel S/o Sh. Ramji Lal Goel was the vendorcumproprietor of M/s Sunil Trading Company, who was also the Incharge and responsible for the day to day conduct of the business of the said shop.

Further the sample commodity i.e. Gutkha was manufactured by M/s.
Som Fresheners Pvt. Ltd. (accused no. 2) and it supplied the Gutkha to Sh. Sunil Kumar Goel (accused no. 1).

M/s. Som Fresheners Pvt. Ltd. has appointed Sh. Hari Mohan Mathur (accused no.
2) as its nominee and as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of business of M/s.
Son Fresheners Pvt. Ltd.
M/s. Som Fresheners Pvt. Ltd being a company is also liable.

3 It is further the prosecution's case that the sample was sent to Public Analyst for analysis and as per the report of Public Analyst the sample was misbranded because language of statutory warning is not as per the language of Rule 42 of PFA Rules.

Accordingly, after obtaining the necessary Sanction/
Consent under Section 20 of the PFA Act, the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of section 2 (ix) (k) of the PFA Act r/w Rule 42 of PFA Rules which is punishable under section 16 (1) (a) read with Sec. 7 of the PFA Act, 1954.
4 After the complaint was filed, the accused was summoned vide order dated 10.07.2006.

5 Notice for violation of provisions of section 2 (ix) (k) of the PFA Act r/w Rule 42 of PFA Rules which is punishable under section 16 (1) (a) read with Sec. 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 was framed against the accused persons vide order dated 25.11.2009 to which accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
6 Statements U/sec. 313 Cr. P.C. of the accused persons namely M/s. Som Freshners Pvt. Ltd.

through its AR Sh. V.K. Bansal and accused Sunil Kumar Goel were recorded on 05.10.2013 and accused Hari Mohan Mathur was recorded on 17.04.2013, wherein the accused persons claimed themselves to be innocent.
Despite opportunity, accused persons did not lead any Da vs . Sunil Kr. Goel Page 1/9 on 12 February, 2016

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110129648/
2 defence evidence.

A brief scrutiny of the evidence recorded in the matter is as under:
7 PW 1 F.I. Sh. V.P.S. Chaudhary, deposed on 09.01.2006 he along with FA Balwant Shah with other officials of the PFA department under the supervision and directions of SDM/LHA, Sh K K Sharma visited the premises of M/s Sunil Trading Company,
N27, Vishnu Garden, New Delhi where the accused Sunil Kumar Goel was found conducting the business of food articles there for sale ready for sale for human consumption including Gutkha in original sealed packet bearing identical label declaration.
He deposed that they disclosed their identity and intention for purchasing of Gutkha (Ready for sale), for analysis to which the accused agreed.

He deposed that before purchasing the sample, PW1 tried his best to procure some public witness by requesting some customers, passersby and neighbouring shopkeepers but as none agreed and on his request, FA Balwant Shah agreed and joined as a witness at about 6.00 pm.

He deposed that he purchased 9x136gms of sealed packets of Gutkha bearing identical label declaration on payment of Rs. 387/
vide vendor's receipt Ex PW1/A.

He deposed that he divided the sample into three equal parts by putting one originally sealed packet in one counter part and each counter part containing the sample of Gutkha was separately packed, fastened,
marked and sealed according to PFA Act and rules.

He deposed that LHA slips bearing his code number and signature were affixed on each counter and signature of the vendor obtained in such a manner that partly appeared on the LHA slip as well as on the wrapper of the sample bottle.

He deposed that Notice in Form VI Ex. PW1/B was prepared and the label was reproduced in Form VI and a copy was given to the accused as per his endorsement at portion A to A bearing his signature at point A.
He deposed that Panchnama Ex PW1/C was prepared.

He further deposed that the remaining two counter parts of sample in intact condition along with two copies of Memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited at point A and that of LHA on 10.01.2016 vide receipt Ex PW1/E and that of LHA at point B which he identified with the intimation that one counter part of the sample in intact condition has already been deposited with the PA.
He deposed that all the copies of Memo of Form VII were marked with the impression of seal which was used to seal the sample counter parts.
He deposed that on receipt of the PA report Ex PW1/F, according to which the sample was found misbranded as statutory warning was not as per Rule 42 of PFA Rules, as mentioned at portion X.
He deposed that he further investigated the matter.
He deposed that he sent a letter Ex PW1/G to the vendor and received its reply Ex PW1/G1 that he purchased the sample commodity from M/s Som Fresheners Pvt Ltd., Ghaziabad, UP.

PW1 also sent a letter Ex PW1/H to STO Ward no. 57 to disclose the constitution of M/s Sunil Trading Company and as per its reply at portion A, Sh Sunil Kumar Goel was found to be a sole proprietor of M/s. Sunil Trading Company.
He deposed that he received reply Ex PW1/J along with photocopy of Memorandum of Article of Association, copy of Form VIII of Nominee Sh Hari Mohan Mathur, the same are mark X and Y.
He deposed that he also sent a letter Ex PW1/K to CMO, Ghaziabad to confirm the nomination and received its reply Ex PW1/K1 along with photocopy of Nomination form mark Y.

He deposed that after completion of the investigation by him, the complete case file along with all the statutory documents were sent to the Director Sh K. S. Wahi through LHA, who after Da vs . Sunil Kr. Goel Page 1/9 on 12 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110129648/
3
going through the entire case file, applied his mind and gave the sanction for prosecution Ex PW1/L against the accused persons.
He deposed that he identified the signature of K S Wahi at point A on Ex PW1/L.
He deposed that the complaint Ex PW1/M was filed in court by him.
He deposed that the intimation letter PW1/N along with PA report was sent to the accused persons by registered post through LHA which was not received back undelivered.
He deposed that the postal registration receipt copy is Ex PW1/O. 8
During his crossexamination by accused no. 1 to 3, he stated that each pouch was not separately weighed.
He stated that the sample packets were closed packets and there was no separate seat affixed on the packets.

He stated that he prepared the Report under Rule 9 (e)
at the spot.
He stated that he did not mention on the documents prepared at the spot that he observed any abnormality on the label of the sample commodity.
He stated that the contents of the label was reproduced by him on the notice in Form VI.
He stated that he did not discuss the facts of this case with the Director, PFA.
He stated that Public Analyst mentioned in her report that the sample commodity was not complying with the Rule 42.
He stated that he has not mentioned the details as to how the warning was not complying with the Rule 42 in the complaint.
He stated that on that day, his posting was in subdivision Patel Nagar and he was incharge and responsible Food Inspector of Patel Nagar.
He stated that no other FI was posted there.
He stated that Intimation Letter alongwith PA Report was sent through Regd. Post but not personally served.
He stated that no acknowledgment of receiving the intimation letter alongwith PA report is on the judicial record.
He denied that the intimation letter alongwith PA report was not received by the accused persons.
He stated that he had not mentioned in the complaint that in what manner the warning given by the accused was causing prejudice to the consumers.
9 This so far is the evidence in the matter.
10 I have carefully considered the submissions of both sides and perused the record meticulously.
11 The accused persons are facing the allegations of violating the provision provided under section 2 (ix) (k) of the PFA Act for contravening Rule 42 of PFA Rules .

As per the report of Public Analyst ,
the sample of "Gutkha" was misbranded because statutory warning was not given thereon as per the language of Rule 42 of PFA Rules.
Accused no. 1 is the Vendor of sample commodity and the accused no. 3 is the Manufacturer of which the accused no. 2 is the Nominee.
The accused no. 3 supplied the sample commodity to accused no. 1. 12
The star / the material witness of the prosecution i.e. Food Inspector Sh. V.P.S Choudhary proved the sample proceedings dated 09.01.2006 as were conducted in the presence of SDM/LHA.

From the deposition of the prosecution witness (PW 1) coupled with documents Ex. PW1/ A to C i.e. Vendor's receipt, Notice Form VI and panchnama as proved by the prosecution, the admissions made by the accused persons during their examination under Section 313 Cr. P.C. as recorded before the Ld. Predecessor of this Court which are admissible in evidence against the accused persons in view of sub clause (4) of Section 313 Cr. P C, no doubt remains that the sample of Gutkha was indeed collected by the Food Inspector for analysis from premises of M/s Sunil Trading Company of which accused Sunil Kumar Goel is the vendor and incharge of and responsible for conduct of day to day business of the above said M/s. Sunil Trading Company.
The procedural formality for lifting the sample were also duly adhere to as reflected from the testimony of PW 1 . 13

Section 2 (ix) reads to the effect that 'an article of food shall be deemed to be misbranded if it is not labelled in accordance with the requirements of this act or Rules made Da vs . Sunil Kr. Goel Page 1/9 on 12 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110129648/
4 thereunder'.

The article in question is a 'Gutkha'; the sample of which was adjudged positive for Nicotine test and was also having therein 'betel nut' as an ingredient, meaning thereby that it was a tobacco product containing supari/betel nut as well.

A sample of the given article in respect of its labelrequirements is required to be adjudged in the light of the Provision under Rule 42 (zzz) &
(zzz) (6).

These provisions are being reproduced hereunder:
Rule 42 (zzz) [ " Every package of chewing tobacco shall bear the following label,
namelyChewing of tobacco is injurious to health".] Rule 42 (zzz) (6) [" Every packages of supari and advertisement relating thereto shall carry the following warning in conspicuous and bold print namely - Chewing of Supari is Injurious to Health"]
14 It is important to note that no standard of Gutkha is prescribed under the PFA Act and the PFA Rules.
The Notice in Form VI Ex. PW1/B does bear the reproduction of the label declaration drawn from the sealed Gutkha pouches.
The said label declaration does contain the statutory warning to the effect that 'chewing of tobacco and supari is injurious to health'.
The prosecution has in no way been able to establish as to how and why the declaration on the label of the sample commodity was violative of Rule 42 of PFA Rules.
The PFA Rules in general and Rule 42 in particular, are entirely silent as to the language which is to be used if, both Tobacco and Supari are the ingredients of a particular food article.

It nowhere specifies as to whether in that situation, the statutory warning as under Rule 42 (ZZZ) and Rule 42 (ZZZ) (6) are to be written separately or the warning is to be expressed in a single sentence combining the warning prescribed under Rule 42 (ZZZ) and Rule 42 (ZZZ) (6), as is done in the present case.
I am of the opinion that either way, the same meaning would be conveyed.
It is to be borne in mind that the purpose of prescribing labelling condition under PFA Act and Rules is to empower the consumer to take informed decision.

The consumer in no way is prejudiced by the warning given by the accused persons on the label of sample commodity as same meaning is conveyed that chewing of Supari as well as Tobacco is injurious to health.
So the accused persons are not found guilty of contravening section 2 (ix)(k) of PFA Act and Rule 42 of PFA Rules, and stand acquitted.
Announced in the open Court [PRIYA MAHENDRA]
